sources.label: Seifel Consulting for the Mayor's Office of Housing, "Inclusionary Housing Financial Analysis", December 2012, Figure 3 "Comparison of 2012 Parking Costs Per Unit, City of San Francisco" (source line: TAC, developer pro formas, general contractors, Seifel)
sources.page: report p. 15 (PDF p. 18), Figure 3, bars "Podium Parking"

podium.method: Hard construction cost per space, 2012 dollars. Figure 3 is a bar chart of cost per unit at 0.75 and 1.0 spaces per unit; the bar tops were measured from the embedded chart image against its $10,000 gridlines (pixel scale 272.4 px per $10,000): podium $21,531 per unit at 0.75 and $28,689 at 1.0, so $28,708 and $28,689 per space; rounded to $28,700 (about +/- $200 from the measurement). Not escalated: dollarsYear 2012 is before 2024 and is flagged for the owner in docs/dev/cars-data.md.

sources.label: Strategic Economics for the San Francisco Planning Department, memo "Analysis of Inclusionary Housing and Community Facilities District for Hub Properties", 2017-01-18, Appendix A, Figure 16 "Hard Cost Assumptions" (Source: Strategic Economics, 2016)
sources.page: pp. 20-21 (PDF pp. 20-21): text "an across-the-board cost assumption of $80,000 per space. This cost reflects the fact that most or all parking would be located underground"; Figure 16 row "Parking, Per space, $80,000"

belowGrade.method: Hard construction cost per space as stated, 2016 dollars (Figure 16's source line). The memo models a subterranean garage, conventional or with stackers, from interviews with four SF developers and an automated-parking vendor. Not escalated: dollarsYear 2016 is before 2024 and is flagged for the owner in docs/dev/cars-data.md.

sources.page: RSP Final Report p. 7 (PDF p. 173): "parking is supplied at 1.4 spaces per dwelling unit but is only used at about 1 space/unit"; p. i: "supply 40% more parking than is actually utilized"

supplyOverUse.method: Literature (tier 3): 1.4 spaces supplied per 1.0 used, the King County average over about 200 multifamily buildings. SF per-project supply counts exist (Planning Department Records - Projects, data.sf.gov qvu5-m3a2, parking_spaces_prop by record) but no SF per-project count of spaces used was found, so no SF ratio (tier 0-2) can be formed here; see docs/dev/cars-data.md.
